reviews.title: Pretty nice little PC status monitor once you get the hang of the software.
reviews.comment: Its a pretty nice little PC status monitor once you get the hang of the software. Pros- - The case appears to be aluminum and of decent quality but not exceptional/high-end. - The screen itself is good resolution for the size, and does an good job of displaying uploaded videos. - The software isn't super intuitive, but overall it does what it needs to in my situation and I've only had one instance of it crashing or not working properly. - With some patience to fiddle around with the different monitors, and some basic understanding of photo editing software some pretty cool custom results are possible with the theme editor and video display functions. - Some of the provided themes are pretty decent and can be a good starting point for a custom theme if you're not as comfortable with photo editing software. Cons- - Only one mounting screw point is provided on the back of the screen case, and in my situation the screen can't be mounted inside my PC case cleanly because of this. If they had provided even just one more mounting point it likely could've worked as I initially intended, in any case I ended up setting it up on my desk anyways and that is probably the more convenient way to actually use the screen as a PC status monitor for my situation. -Color accuracy isn't the best but with a little tweaking you can get colors on screen to match pretty well with your PC screen or RGB or whatever it is you want to match. - The software is not intuitive, although the provided videos are indeed helpful in learning more about the theme editing. For some, having to edit their own transparencies to get a certain look might be too much work, or beyond their skill. Overall, I'm not sure it's worth $70, but it is really quite good. If you're not interested in paying $60 a year for software (AIDA) and want something with somewhat decent and customizable software, this is probably the best choice. Still gets 5 stars because there isn't really any competition at a reasonable price point like this.
reviews.author: Ryan

reviews.title: So far, so good.
reviews.comment: The built-in themes are decent and work fine out of the box, but the real value for me is in the customization. I was able to create my own themes with gauges and status bars laid out exactly how I wanted, which made it much more useful for my setup. Everything that was advertised came in the box. It also included two magnetic strips, which made for a very clean and easy installation inside my case. Overall, it does what it’s supposed to do. If you want a customizable internal system monitor and don’t mind spending a little time setting it up the way you like, it’s a solid option.
reviews.author: Zac

reviews.title: Pretty good product, even when on the pricier side
reviews.comment: Very nice little screen.  Love that it comes with a USB-A to USB-C cable as well as a 4-pin connector (screen side) and a USB2.0 header on the other side to connect directly to the motherboard.  Also comes with a bracket and a single screw that will allow you to screw it into a screw hole on a case fan to mount it in your case. I decided to 3M Command Strip stick it to the front of my case and run the 4-pin connector to USB2.0 header cable through one of the vent holes and connect it to my motherboard.  Can't see the cable at all and gives me all the stats I need. You can see the other reviews that shows a lot of the "preinstalled" themes.  I decided to make a simple one (in my picture and video) that gives me the information I need.  The software for the screen is pretty basic but lets you make your old themes.  You can even upload videos (make sure to use the included MicroSD card so you have space if you want to use videos) that will play/loop and even use them as the background with info stuff on top of it.  You can also adjust the brightness from the software and it can get pretty dim to decently bright. I'm giving it 4 out of 5 stars because the price is riding the edge of being justifiable.  If it was touchscreen, it would be worth the price, but it is not.  The software seems kind of thrown together as well and doesn't give me the option for some of the items I would like.  For example, from my layout I use, the Power bars won't let me set a max value, so when my RTX 5090 uses over 500w, it goes past end of the bar.  When creating my theme as well, I had to make sure to save it quite often as sometimes the software would just crash and if I didn't save it, I would have to start over.

reviews.title: Worked ok till software update
reviews.comment: 12/22/22 update. It worked fine till the latest software update. Now on everyboot the software is removed from my pc and I have to extract the files again. This is suspect behavior and was already sketched out by the software to begin with. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- I was tired of alt tabbing to see my sensors on HWinfo so I decided to be bougie and buy this. Install will be easy if you are familiar with your pc's mobo and know where the usb headers are I had to buy an "NZXT usb header hub." Don't forget the "USB header to USB cable adapter." The app you have to download stays running in the background for the monitor which is basic but it would have been nice to utilized the pi and make the software onboard for the monitor. The Software is easy to work until you get into the editing portion. At first glance it is a nightmare but Im sure with time it will become easier. The preset that come with the software are fine I just wish there was an option to customize the color location and sensors. IF there is an option it isn't ui friendly. All in all I'm not upset with the purchase. It definitely isn't worth the price tag though. Id say 25-35$ max would be fair for what it is.
